headline: Pentagon Routes All Strike Cables Through National Nickname Prayer Board
deck: Eastern Ohio Dave Threat Desk Now Requires Double Supplications for Any Envelope Lacking Further Identification
article:
The Department of Defense confirmed Thursday that strike-authorization cables will now pass through the National Nickname Prayer Board before delivery. Officials cited a recent swap in which a cable addressed to Dave in State reached Dave in Logistics instead, prompting an unintended escalation that the department now treats as official justification for further action.

Mail-sorting facilities have expanded the Eastern Ohio Dave Threat Desk to handle the volume from the state's forty thousand residents sharing the name. Staff sort correspondence by nickname, physical description, and prayer when no additional markers appear on the envelope. Spokesman Dave the Tall One stated that personnel now pray twice whenever an item lists only Dave, adding that the practice has reduced delivery errors to an acceptable rate for routine operations.

The misrouted cable in question carried instructions for a limited response and arrived at the wrong recipient with the notation deliver anyway, He knows which one stamped across the header. Logistics processed the document as received, leading to the sequence of events now cited in subsequent authorizations. The board has since issued guidance requiring all cables to include at least one additional descriptor or risk automatic referral to the prayer protocol.

Defense contractors have begun printing standard forms with fields for nickname, approximate height, and preferred prayer duration to meet the new routing requirements.
author: By Morgan Ellis, National Security Desk

oped.title: Prayer Boards Prove Our Military Genius—Blame the Undevout Daves
oped.author: Reverend Buckminster 'Bucky' Dave III, PhD in Postal Theology and Honorary Eastern Ohio Threat Desk Chaplain
oped.body: The Pentagon’s decision to funnel every strike cable through the National Nickname Prayer Board is not a bureaucratic embarrassment but a triumph of adaptive faith. In a nation of forty thousand identical Daves, last names would have been a godless crutch anyway. Double supplications for unmarked envelopes simply ensure the right Dave receives his righteous payload while the slothful receive divine spam. Critics who moan about delays forget that prayer builds character, and character builds precision bombing. I myself once had a perfectly legitimate grudge cable rerouted to a different Dave because some lazy clerk offered only single supplication; the resulting friendly fire incident was entirely that clerk’s moral failure, not mine. Rather than dismantle this elegant system, we should mandate triple prayers and a mandatory hat tax on anyone whose nickname lacks sufficient vowels. Efficiency through piety is the only path forward.

stories.headline: Cleveland PD Requires Double Supplications on All Dave-Related Warrants
stories.deck: Eastern Ohio desk now logs 340 daily prayer slips for repeat offenders sharing the same moniker
stories.article:
The Cleveland Police Department has aligned its warrant system with the Pentagon's nickname board after three mistaken detentions in a single week. Officers must now submit two nicknames and a formal supplication for any envelope lacking further details, with mailroom staff routing forms through the same Eastern Ohio prayer volunteers used for strike cables.

Processing time for routine burglary reports has risen from four hours to eleven, though the department credits the change with a 19 percent drop in Dave-on-Dave misidentifications at county lockups.

stories.headline: Minor League Baseball Clubs Add Prayer Board to Dugout Scorecards
stories.deck: All-Dave pitching staffs force new rule on distinguishing relief appearances by nickname alone
stories.article:
The Akron RubberDucks have installed a laminated nickname board beside the dugout after four consecutive games featured lineup cards listing three Daves in the same batting order. Umpires now require a verified moniker and single supplication before crediting any hit or strikeout to the correct player.

League statisticians report that home-run totals for "Dave from the tool shop" rose 27 percent once the board went live, while errors attributed to "Dave the lefty" dropped to near zero.

stories.headline: Ohio Manufacturers Bill Customers by Nickname After Invoice Mail Failures
stories.deck: Local firms report 62 percent of supplier payments delayed until prayer volunteers confirm the correct Dave
stories.article:
Akron tool-and-die shops have begun printing invoices with two nicknames and a suggested prayer instead of traditional addresses. Accounts payable clerks at three plants now route every envelope through the regional nickname board before cutting checks, citing repeated returns from sorting halls that could not distinguish between "Dave who ordered the gaskets" and "Dave who signed the contract."

One firm recorded a 41-day average payment cycle on parts shipments, prompting managers to assign a full-time volunteer to compose supplications matching each customer's preferred moniker.
